schema_note: Every number in this file is real and independently reproducible -- computed from actual sacrebleu runs, actual verification-pipeline state files, or actual dataset files in the lao-thai-translator repo. Nothing here is estimated, projected, or hand-typed as a round number. Fields with a null value mean 'not measured under this methodology,' never 'assumed good.'

generations.label: Generation 3
generations.release_notes: The DPO-trained checkpoint produced by an earlier 5-step sanitization-pipeline retrain. Superseded after we identified what we internally call the 'Generation 3 crisis': a cycle-consistency blind spot where a forward and reverse translation model can share a bias that round-trips cleanly while being confidently wrong about the actual meaning. That specific failure mode is the reason Generation 4's verification system (below) uses back-translation as only one of two independent checks, never the sole gate. We don't show chrF++/BLEU scores for Generation 3 -- it predates this project's current benchmark suites, and we'd rather show nothing than a number we didn't actually measure.

generations.label: Generation 4 (current, live)

reference_benchmark.methodology: sacrebleu corpus_chrf (word_order=2) / corpus_bleu (tokenize=char) against 100 human-reference translation pairs per domain, 5 domains total. Model-level quality signal, not a per-movie score.

defect_categories_fixed: Garbled decoder artifact (a bare "ແມ" token left as an incomplete fragment, never finished into a real word)
Repetition / stutter artifacts (e.g. a phrase's opening words duplicated back-to-back)
"Cat" hallucination (a garbled token completed into the unrelated real word for "cat")
"Interfere" hallucination (the real word for "interfere/intervene" substituted for unrelated content -- the single largest defect pattern found in this project)
Code-mixing (untranslated English words left stranded inside otherwise-Lao sentences)
Numeral errors (e.g. "100 thousand" rendered as "ten thousand")

generations.release_notes: Every one of the 287 published movies was independently re-verified, cue by cue, using a Double-Lock Back-Translation Consensus system. Lock 1 is a set of deterministic Lao-text filters built and refined by hand as each new failure pattern was found. Lock 2 is an English-only back-translation semantic-equivalence judge -- the model is never shown its own Lao output to grade, precisely because that self-referential check is what caused the Generation 3 crisis. A correction is written only when BOTH locks independently agree. This process confirmed 7,251 corrections. The largest single defect found was a hallucinated substitution of the real Lao word for 'interfere' standing in for unrelated content -- 654 raw occurrences found corpus-wide; a dedicated cleanup pass fixed only 15 of those (2.6%), confirming most instances are a stable model bias rather than a one-off translation slip. That known limitation is left undisturbed in the published corpus rather than papered over, pending a future targeted retrain.

generations.label: Generation 5 (in preparation)
generations.release_notes: Training has not started yet. The Generation 5 DPO dataset has been staged from Generation 4's own 7,251 verified corrections: deduplicated by prompt (2,127 duplicates dropped, keeping the first occurrence of each), split 90/10 into 4,611 training examples and 513 validation examples. We publish performance numbers only after they're actually measured against a trained checkpoint -- this entry intentionally has no scores yet, and won't until a real retrain has run.
